headline: Recommended a land bank application for affordable housing to the mayor, scoring it 97 points.
summary: Members discussed adding accessible, ADA-compliant unit requirements to future contracts, and staff will research how to do it. The land bank project would start by checking whether a land bank fund is legally and financially feasible. Maynard Homes Phase 2 and Avery Lane Apartments are seeking funding, and about $1.5 million would remain if both get their full requests.
decisions: Recommended the land bank application to the mayor, 3-0 with one abstention.
Asked city staff to research how to add accessible unit requirements and present it at the next meeting.

decision_titles: Land bank application for affordable housing
Staff research on accessible units in future contracts
plain_text:
COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES 
 
OCTOBER 12TH, 2026 
ROOM 208, CITY HALL 
229 MAIN STREET, NASHUA, NH 03060 
 
Members Present: Matt Sullivan, Liz Hannum, Kristy Besada, Skye Wheeler, Lori Wilshire 
Staff Present: Jessica Connors 
 
Call to Order 
M. Sullivan called the meeting to order at 5:05PM as quorum was present. 
 
Discussion: Scoring Procedures 
• Point minimums were discussed; the committee will confirm what the point minimums were set at before 
the next meeting. Several members commented that they’ve tried to create a high level of consistency with 
the committee, but that the points could be set aside if needed; they are meant to be guidelines. 
Discussion: Contract Updates 
• S. Wheeler proposed introducing a stipulation to future contracts that will encourage developers to include 
more accessible/ADA-compliant units in their properties. He stated that it’s significantly easier to make units 
ADA-compliant from the very start, as opposed to adding accessibility features once tenants already live in 
the units.  
• S. Wheeler reminded committee members that individuals can become disabled at any point, and that 
many unhoused individuals are disabled. He added that creating more accessible units might shorten 
housing waiting lists overall.  
• L. Hannum requested clarification on how S. Wheeler sees this being incorporated into committee 
recommendations.  
• M. Sullivan mentioned that they had talked about adding universal design as a potential requirement in the 
past, and that could be reconsidered.  
• S. Wheeler stated that the scope of this recommendation would require further conversation and that he 
does not necessarily have the answer but would like it to be a discussion point going forward.  
• L. Hannum proposed that city staff members research the best way to possible implement this suggestion 
and present it at the next committee meeting. The other committee members agreed that it should be 
added to the agenda. 
 
• Non-Public Session – Marguerite’s Place 
• S. Wheeler made a motion to go into a non-public session to discuss matters which if discussed in public 
could potentially or would likely affect adversely the reputation of any person other than a member of this 
public body pursuant with RSA 91A(3)(2)(C). 
i. L. Wilshire offered a Second to the motion. 
ii. A roll call was taken, which resulted as follows: 
1. Yea: 5  
2. Nay: 0 
Motion Carried
• Scoring of Land Bank Application 
• M. Sullivan stated that he would like to move on to scoring the land bank study, noting that L. Hannum 
would not vote, but that she would be participatory in the conversation. L. Hannum agreed that she would 
abstain from voting. 
• K. Besada asked if there was a quorum without S. Wheeler present. M. Sullivan clarified that yes, there was 
a quorum present, and additionally noted that at the end of the day, the committee is only responsible for 
recommending projects to the Mayor. 
• L. Hannum provided a quick summary of the project, which will be split into two parts:  
i. Part One: Determining if it’s legally and financially feasible to create a land bank fund that would 
purchase land and then bid it out for affordable housing. 
ii. Part Two: If it is determined to be feasible, part two would further flesh out the idea, including the 
recommended structure and where it could live — in this committee, or in another group. 
• K. Besada asked if the full amount of the request would be spent even if the project was determined not 
to be feasible; L. Hannum clarified that it would be. 
• L. Hannum noted that similar land banks exist, but that they’re on conservation land. M. Sullivan noted 
that it might be best to have a nonprofit do this. 
• The committed scored the project as follows: 
i. Program Team Capacity: 17 points 
ii. Project Sustainability: 15 points 
iii. Financial Feasibility: 15 points 
iv. Project Timeline: 15 points 
v. Organizational Partnerships: N/A, counted as 15 points 
vi. Project Innovation: 10 points 
vii. Community Impact: N/A, counted as 10 points 
viii. Bonus Points: N/A, counted as 0 points 
ix. Final Score: 97 
 
• Vote – Land Bank Application 
• L. Wilshire made a motion to approve the project and recommend it to the mayor. 
i. K. Besada offered a Second to the motion. 
ii. A roll call was taken, which resulted as follows: 
1. Yea: 3 
2. Abstained: 1  
3. Nay: 0 
Motion Carried 
Discussion: Upcoming Projects & Committee Funding 
• M. Sullivan noted that the committee’s remaining funding is limited, and gave a brief summary of two 
upcoming projects seeking funding: Maynard Homes Phase 2, sponsored by the Nashua Housing 
Authority, and Avery Lane Apartments, sponsored by Tamposi Brothers Development. 
• M. Sullivan stated that if the full awards requested were given to these two projects, the committee would 
have approximately $1.5 million dollars left in funding.  
• M. Sullivan will contact Tamposi Brothers Development about potentially presenting their project at the 
next committee meeting. 
Discussion: Next Committee Meeting 
• M. Sullivan, L. Hannum, and J. Connors have a conflicting event on November 9 th, the next scheduled 
committee day. 
• November 12th was proposed as an alternative meeting date; J. Connors will reach out to determine if this 
date works for everyone. 
 
• Meeting adjourned at 7:00PM.  
 
• Next meeting: The next meeting date is under discussion.
